data.long_meaning: Ramavatar translates to 'Rama's Protector' in Sanskrit and Hindi. 'Rama' refers to the popular Hindu deity, Lord Rama, who embodies the ideals of righteousness, duty, and love. historical_references.reference: Ramavatar was a title conferred upon Ramachandra, a renowned king of the Solar Dynasty in Hindu mythology. He is most famously known as Lord Rama, the hero of the Indian epic Ramayana.

Ramavatar II was a Rajput king of the Chauhan dynasty in the 12th century AD, who ruled over the regions of Gujarat and Malwa in present-day India. He is known for his military prowess and is said to have expanded his kingdom significantly during his reign.

seo.description_paragraph: Ramavatar is a name of great cultural and religious significance in Hinduism. Derived from the Sanskrit words 'Rama' and 'Vatar', the name Ramavatar translates to 'God in the form of Vishnu'. This name is believed to be bestowed upon individuals who are destined to lead a virtuous life and uphold the values of truth, righteousness, and selflessness. The name Ramavatar holds a special place in Hindu mythology, as it is the name of a popular deity, Lord Rama, who is considered an avatar of Vishnu. In Hindu culture, the name Ramavatar is often given to newborn boys as a mark of respect and reverence for the deity. Today, the name Ramavatar is popular not only in India but also among the Hindu diaspora around the world.
